content_voiceover: This table is one of the highest-yield summaries for immune hemolytic anemia on the boards. Warm AIHA is most common, about half to seventy percent of cases, with DAT usually IgG positive, sometimes IgG plus C3, mediated by IgG antibodies against Rh antigens, and both eluate and plasma show panagglutinin activity. Cold agglutinin disease, sixteen to thirty-two percent, has a DAT positive for C3 only — because IgM fixes complement then detaches — so the eluate is non-reactive but plasma remains panagglutinin reactive, with specificity against the I antigen. Mixed AIHA combines both patterns, roughly seven to eight percent. Paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria, rare in adults but up to thirty-two percent in children, also shows a C3-only DAT, but the plasma antibody is a unique IgG biphasic hemolysin — the Donath-Landsteiner antibody — targeting the P antigen. Drug-induced immune hemolytic anemia, twelve to eighteen percent, typically shows an IgG-positive DAT with Rh specificity, mimicking warm AIHA. The key exam pearl: a C3-only DAT with a non-reactive eluate points you toward cold agglutinin disease or PCH rather than warm AIHA, and PCH is distinguished by its classic biphasic Donath-Landsteiner hemolysin against the P antigen, often seen post-virally in children.
keypoints: WAIHA (48-70%): DAT usually IgG with or without C3, IgG antibody, Rh specificity.
CAD (16-32%): DAT C3 only, IgM antibody, non-reactive eluate, anti-I specificity.
PCH: rare in adults, up to 32% in children; C3-only DAT with the Donath-Landsteiner biphasic IgG hemolysin against the P antigen.
Drug-induced (12-18%): DAT IgG positive, Rh specificity, mimics WAIHA.
C3-only DAT with a non-reactive eluate should make you think cold agglutinin disease or PCH, not warm AIHA.
keypoint_voiceover: Five exam pearls from this table. Warm AIHA is the most common type, with an IgG-positive DAT and Rh antibody specificity. Cold agglutinin disease shows a C3-only DAT, a non-reactive eluate, and anti-I specificity, because IgM detaches after fixing complement. Paroxysmal cold hemoglobinuria is rare in adults but important in children, also with a C3-only DAT, but distinguished by the Donath-Landsteiner biphasic hemolysin targeting the P antigen. Drug-induced immune hemolytic anemia mimics warm AIHA with an IgG-positive DAT and Rh specificity. And the biggest testable pearl: whenever you see a C3-only DAT with a non-reactive eluate, think cold agglutinin disease or PCH, not warm AIHA.
